July & September 2023Golden Gate Canyon & Breckenridge, Colorado

Rocky Mountain Summer

memories below

Hand to Horizon

Some of the best views in the Rockies are knee high. One July afternoon I walked through an aspen grove in Golden Gate Canyon State Park, in the foothills west of Golden. A rocky summit stood over the treetops, and the forest floor was in bloom. Colorado blue columbines grew in the shade among the ferns, their lavender-blue sepals flaring around white petals and a puff of yellow stamens. Columbine comes from the Latin word for dove, and the sepals do look a bit like wings. An orange wallflower stood out against the pale aspen trunks, and a lone white geranium sat quietly in the greenery.

On the first weekend of September I looked up for a change. I hiked the Mohawk Lakes trail south of Breckenridge, past a stepped waterfall tumbling through rust-colored rock, and climbed toward the lakes above. In one basin a huge bare dome of scree rose over a tangle of willow and spruce and made everything else look small. Farther on, a clear lake lay beneath a slope of broken rock streaked with what looked like old snow. The sky was split in two, with bright cumulus over the valley and a heavy gray lid over the water. Pack a rain shell, because the weather up high turns fast.

I was still out there when the light went blue. A small pond among the boulders and spruce held the last of the sky, and on its far side a fire glowed between the trees, its orange doubled in the water. In July, summer fit in the palm of my hand. By September it filled an entire basin.
